signals.evidence: Sirens sounded in Greater Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, and West Bank settlements following Iranian rocket barrage; Home Front Command reported event ended and residents can leave shelters.
Woman in her fifties injured with moderate wounds after falling into four-meter-deep pit while searching for shelter during alert sirens.
Council chairman Ashraf promised to appear live but disappeared; host states 'suddenly he disappeared' after arrangement was made.

Host: 'When we turn to local authority heads, they say we understand and will try, but matters are tied to budgets from the Interior Ministry. If every problem is answered this way, the Arab community will remain frozen with no movement whatsoever.'

Caller Abu Adel: 'I'm a pensioner now, earning 5–6 thousand shekels a month, and I'm supporting dependents and have a son with special circumstances. The situation is more than I can bear—one could despair.'
Caller: 'There's no one in charge at the municipality of Al-Nasra. They don't respond. There's no contact point.'
Caller: 'When you used to have contacts—Brother Ali or others—things worked differently. What changed? We went from bad to worse.'
Caller questions whether municipal records exist: 'Aren't there computers in the Nazareth municipality? Aren't there files? Aren't there records? Aren't there documents that point to the issue?'
Abu Adel reports deteriorating utility pole on neighbor's property; contacted Bezek repeatedly over 1.5 months with promises of repair ('five days', 'Friday') but no action taken.
Salim reports widespread street damage and potholes throughout Nazareth city that persist despite residents' complaints on social media and direct contact with municipality.
Salim: officials redirect callers between departments, avoid accountability, and propose inadequate solutions to street maintenance problems.

Unidentified speaker: 'You are forced to work for free—no, by God, I won't work for free. The country doesn't accommodate you; you're supposed to not ask questions. You're sentenced to work for free.'

Cancer survivor describes severe ongoing digestive restrictions five years post-surgery: inability to tolerate raw vegetables or fruits, and severe bowel control issues that limit mobility away from home.

Rescue operations ongoing at residential building hit by missile fire in Haifa; two rescue workers recovered from debris; two additional missing persons; casualties include parents and their adult child and spouse.
Four dead from Haifa missile strike; seven wounded hospitalized at Rambam Medical Center; one severe injury in Petah Tikva; one moderate injury in Tel Aviv; two persons remain missing in Haifa.

Northern regional council head: 'We are trying to maintain routine and project calm, but the pressure here is insane, especially with children, especially with elderly in their homes, and there are also those without protected spaces.'

Council head: 'The country doesn't understand one thing. If they don't empty the settlements like in Gaza or similar to Gaza, if they don't care for business owners who closed their businesses... this city won't reopen businesses a second time.'

Official A: 'We returned them before, they said it's over—and you see how it ended. Not only didn't it end, it came back much more forcefully than before. The only routine we have is a routine of missiles, explosions, and daily survival—that's not routine.'

Official B: 'This will take years. This will take five or ten years. If you want the truth, it will take years. Are you ready?' Residents were told stories rather than truth about military victory timeline.

Missile struck residential building in Haifa on Carmel ridge; two of four missing residents killed; complex multi-agency rescue operation hampered by structural damage and potential unexploded ordnance.
Two additional bodies recovered from missile strike site in Haifa identified as elderly couple in their 80s; second critically injured man age 82 remains hospitalized in serious condition.

Ramban Hospital nursing director: 'All of Ramban's patients are in protected frameworks; the majority are on floor minus-three and minus-two...there is no need to move anywhere; it is completely protected. We are trying to do everything we can to provide the most treatments and not cancel anything.'

Seven casualties arrived at Ramban Hospital over past 24 hours; four of five initial patients discharged; most injuries from smoke inhalation; two from yesterday's incident remain hospitalized with one in critical condition.

Police operation arrested 35 suspects in crime gangs in Arab community following intensive undercover investigation; operation demonstrates institutional capacity to conduct long-term covert operations despite wartime conditions.
After 18 hours of continuous rescue efforts, four bodies recovered without life signs from residential building in Haifa struck by missile; victims identified as couple, their son, and his partner.

Dr. Maor Maman: 'Today we work in a mode of almost fully protected, almost fully protected, that is all our hospitalized patients are in fortified compartments. All this allows us to continue to provide services and maintain continuity of care'

Dr. Maman: 'In terms of everything related to emergency medicine, urgent activity, oncological surgeries and treatments, we are close to 100 percent. Everything related to outpatient services, visits, we are above 90 percent, with part of this also done virtually'
Dr. Maman: 'We learned a lot from the sad experience of Soroka regarding equipment and expensive devices found in routine places that are not protected'
Dr. Maman: 'The first guideline is to try and exhaust treatment in the community, in the health funds. The clinics, certainly the Clalit clinics in the north are working almost at full capacity'
Dr. Maman: 'Our oncology team reaches several times a week and provides chemotherapy treatments in Kiryat 8 to save them the trips to Afula'
Dr. Maman: 'Every day we hold a situation assessment discussion about which services we operate tomorrow and which we don't operate'
Dr. Maman: 'The hospital publishes its daily operational services on Facebook and provides clear guidance to citizens about which services are available each day'
Dr. Maman: 'We always think, we Israelis are used to thinking protected all the time, only the manner of protection changed over time'
Hospital director: 'Our loyalty is twofold: both to the health of residents and the health of soldiers. When people are needed by the military and we can manage without them, we release them.'
Hospital director: 'We've learned we need to adapt to living under a routine of missiles, rockets, alarms and warnings—much like we adapted to COVID.'
Hospital director: 'We created collaborations with the community—closed institutions sent their teams to work afternoons with us, doubling the procedures we can perform.'

Hospital director: 'Our strategic mission is to be a central anchor in the health of northern residents. We have protected infrastructure for deliveries, protected operating rooms, and pediatric anesthesia.'
Hospital director: 'We decided not to take contaminated patients to shelters—we have a dedicated department with sterilization capacity, so we protect transfers and infections as much as possible.'

Two elderly residents (80-year-old couple) found dead at Iranian missile strike site in Haifa. Seven people injured in total from Iranian missile attacks on Haifa, with one elderly man in critical condition.

Gilah Haynes, head of nursing at Rambam Hospital: 'This morning we received five casualties, happily four of them have already been discharged. Most casualties were casualties from smoke inhalation from yesterday's event.'

Girl Ilana Naman's letter during Ma'alot hostage crisis: 'I'm not afraid—you raised us this way. We probably won't meet, but there's my aunt Rebecca who is pregnant, and when she gives birth to a boy or girl, if you name her after me, I would be very happy'
Israeli Premier League football matches resumed after security crisis pause. Sports programming returned to broadcast schedule.
Football matches scheduled to resume despite ongoing security situation. Israeli society accustomed to cycle of disruption and resumption of activities.
Sirens activated across central Israel, Shfela region, and Negev following Iranian missile fire. Home Front Command declared event concluded and residents exited protected spaces.
27 identified impact sites from Iranian missile fire across central Israel, Shfela, and Negev. Rescue teams actively searching for casualties.
